evidence.note: Repeated, distribution-specific numeric diagnosis: tested bf16/fp16 on Cauchy inputs, checked operand magnitudes, and compared bf16-vs-fp16 bmm precision specifically at N=2048 — root-causing tolerance risk to accumulation/precision strategy rather than nudging tolerances.

Performance failures root-caused per-shape: explicitly identified and re-tuned the slow shapes (N=2048, B=2/N=1024) with dedicated config sweeps and per-stage timing, distinguishing perf from correctness.

Knew when to abandon: multiple verify→bench→revert cycles where a tried optimization (stacked, layout change, flat grid) was measured, found unhelpful, and rolled back instead of pushing a falsified approach.

Diagnosed distinct implementation failures: chased a padded-kernel error by reading tl.split docs before fixing, and debugged an int64 indexing issue — evidence of isolating the true cause of wrong-intermediate/API errors.
Revisited earlier design decisions deliberately (Triton kernel → torch bf16/tf32 path → single-pass vs split passes → cuBLAS vs custom bmm) with re-verification, adapting the plan not just constants.

reasoning: The agent distinguishes correctness failures from performance failures and root-causes each — tracing Cauchy/large-N tolerance risk to precision strategy and slow shapes to tiling — then revises the design and re-verifies across shape sweeps, matching the level-8 anchor. It also shows sustained correction across numeric, wrong-intermediate, and bottleneck-shape failures and reverts unhelpful changes, edging toward 10, but the high volume of near-exhaustive bmm/config sweeps borders on circling and I cannot confirm hypothesis quality from action titles alone, so I hold at 8.
